newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: German end-user gas oil stocks static in October.
newsitem.headline: German end-user gas oil stocks static in October.

text.p: Private stocks of heating oil in Germany were static during October, said traders who have seen a confidential monthly report produced for the German oil industry.
The end-user stocks fell a mere 0.1 percent to 64.9 percent of capacity by the end of October, 5.5 percentage points lower than in October 1995.
Western parts of the country, along the Rhine, seemed most prepared for winter with private stocks at 70 percent, up from 68 percent in September.
However, stocks in northern Germany barely increased and those in the southeast fell by three percentage points. Stocks in both areas were at around 63 percent at the end of October.

Traders say German demand was low as prices peaked. In early October, benchmark gas oil futures hit $250.00 a tonne three times, their highest level since February 1991. Over the month, barge prices in the Rotterdam market averaged $235-$240 fob ARA.
"German demand was good in September. It was very bad last month. Some people had clearly stocked up, but some just did not want to buy at those prices," one German trader said.
